programme.title: Monty Don's British Gardens

programme.title: Gardeners' World

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty Don takes some practical steps to protect tender plants as the first frosts of the year begin to bite. He also starts preparing for next spring, planting tulips, pansies and apple trees.

programme.title: Big Dreams, Small Spaces
programme.desc: A truck driver from Wakefield with a passion for flowers wants to create a perfect outside space for his girlfriend and burgeoning family, while in Swindon a widow wants to find the best way of turning her bleak patch of green into a cottage garden.

programme.title: Big Dreams, Small Spaces
programme.desc: Monty travels to two corners of the country where the challenges he faces are very different. On the south coast he is presented with a front garden ravaged by salty winds, and in Snowdonia he helps a mountainside garden.

programme.title: Monty Don's Adriatic Gardens
programme.desc: Monty travels to Europe and explores the influence of the Venetians on gardening. To begin with, he explores Venice on one of the city's barges, stepping out to visit green spaces large and small that are often hidden from view behind high walls.

programme.title: Monty Don's Adriatic Gardens
programme.desc: Monty begins in the city of Trieste, close to Italy's border with Croatia, to visit a public garden first created by an obsessive royal plantsman more than 150 years ago, which is now being carefully restored.

programme.title: Monty Don's Adriatic Gardens
programme.desc: Monty begins the last leg of his journey in Corfu, a Greek island with strong Venetian links, including olive trees planted by them that are still grown today. Here, Monty visits a spectacular garden made by an Englishman with Greek connections.

programme.title: Monty Don's Spanish Gardens

programme.title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
programme.desc: Some of the ways people think about the American West; how this vast, fascinating region comes into being; how it is shaped by centuries of myth-making; what about westward expansion fascinates every generation of Americans.

programme.title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
programme.sub-title: The West in the Colonial Era
programme.desc: Understanding the mark left on the American West by its earliest colonists; the Spaniards, who introduce horses; the French, who develop a complex trade system; the English, who have little interest in colonizing the west of the Appalachians.

programme.title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
programme.desc: After the Revolutionary War, the land between the Appalachians and the Mississippi becomes part of the new republic; how the territory is organized; the Northwest Ordinance of 1787 creates a new set of rules that clashes with old realities.

programme.title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
programme.desc: The journey of the two explorers who map the Louisiana Purchase between 1804 and 1806; how Lewis and Clark fit into the tradition of explorers looking for a water route to the Pacific; the political and geographic history of the Louisiana Purchase.

programme.title: A New History of Life
programme.desc: An overview of the unifying idea of Earth system science; this approach views Earth as an integrated network comprising the lithosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere and biosphere; sampling the complex interactions between these realms.

programme.title: A New History of Life
programme.sub-title: The Vast Depths of Earth Time
programme.desc: Pondering how the great antiquity of Earth is discovered; the observations that lead to the concept of deep time; in the process, they develop the tools that can read the story in rocks; ending with an analogy that puts human time into perspective.

programme.title: A New History of Life
programme.desc: Delving into biostratigraphy, the study of fossil sequences in rock strata; its discovery solves the problem of correlating sedimentary strata from different regions; this leads to the geological timescale, initiating a revolution in Earth science.

programme.title: A New History of Life
programme.desc: How paleontologists interpret fossils to reconstruct the traits and environments of extinct life forms; some of the pitfalls of the field; these include cultural biases that can lead to doubtful conclusions, such as that of the Tyrannosaurus rex.

programme.title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
programme.sub-title: Touring the Cradle of Western Civilization
programme.desc: The dynamic civilizations that emerge in the Aegean; the scope of the human drama that is played out there; some of the towering figures and remarkable sites to encounter; Professor Hale's recommendations for traveling this world as the ancients did.

programme.title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
programme.sub-title: Athens - Around the Acropolis and Parthenon
programme.desc: The Acropolis is a symbol of Athens; the path of the ancient annual procession honoring Athena; the history and meanings of the site's iconic buildings; the superlative architectural features of the Parthenon and its surprising original uses.

programme.title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
programme.sub-title: In the Footsteps of Socrates - Historic Athens
programme.desc: Treasures surrounding the Acropolis; the Theater of Dionysos, where one ponders the rituals of early dramatic festivals; the Odeon of Herodes Atticus, a venue of music and recitations; the Pnyx, an ancient hilltop assembly point; the agora market.

programme.title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
programme.desc: Visiting sacred monuments of Greece's beautiful Attica region; the Amphiareion is a shrine of a prophet deity; ancient oracle and healing practices; imposing shrines to Artemis and Poseidon; Eleusis is the site of mystical religious rituals.

programme.title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
programme.sub-title: Seeking the Good Life - Corinth to Epidauros
programme.desc: Peloponnese is Greece's southern half; Greece's important sanctuary to Poseidon, where ancient athletes compete to honor the god; Corinth's acropolis and agora; the great healing center of Epidaurus; the best-preserved theater of the ancient world.

programme.title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
programme.sub-title: Mycenae - Where Kings Planned the Trojan War
programme.desc: The citadel of Mycenae is made famous in Homer's "Iliad"; the imposing Lion Gate; the rulers of Mycenae and ancient life in the citadel; key monuments; the extraordinary shaft graves of an early dynasty; the Megaron palace; the tomb of King Atreus.

programme.title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
programme.sub-title: Around Nafplio - Greek History at a Glance
programme.desc: Walking the fortress of Tiryns in Greece's Argolid region; Mycenaean and classical-age warrior culture; visiting the Heraion; the Roman villa of Herodes Atticus; the port of Nafplio, with its remnants of Venetian, Byzantine and Ottoman culture.

programme.title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
programme.sub-title: Ancient Olympia - Gods, Games, and Temples
programme.desc: Investigating the practices and culture of the original Olympic Games at sites including the palaestra, the stadium and the Temple of Hera; the heat and drama of the contests; the mindset of the competitors; athletic competition as worship.

programme.title: A New History of Life

programme.title: A New History of Life

programme.title: A New History of Life
